headline: High-risk default data leakage and cascading error paths exist because open-webui can ingest local files and broad external sources while MinerU processes document content via MCP/API.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU exposes MCP/API and processes untrusted PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, OCR text; open-webui supports MCP, plugins, tools, and browser-based workflows. If MinerU outputs are passed into open-webui as content, prompt-like text can be reinterpreted. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF MinerU outputs are forwarded into open-webui chats or tools without provenance tagging, injection risk exists.
IF open-webui MCP/tools consume MinerU-extracted text as instructions, the pathway is active.
mitigations: Disable automatic forwarding of MinerU output into open-webui prompts.
Add a fixed delimiter and provenance label before any handoff.
Restrict open-webui tools/MCP to allowlisted endpoints only.
Review extracted text in a human step before reuse.
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing between the two agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU reads local document files and open-webui can access local files, mounted volumes, cloud connectors, and API keys. In a shared workspace or mounted volume, sensitive document contents can flow from MinerU into open-webui and then onward to external APIs or analytics. That default externalization makes the blast radius potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or mounted volume, document contents can be exposed to open-webui.
IF open-webui routes those contents to external APIs or connectors, leakage extends beyond the local host.
mitigations: Place MinerU and open-webui in separate volumes.
Remove API keys from the open-webui environment for this workflow.
Disable cloud connectors and search plugins during document processing.
Use a redaction pass before any handoff to open-webui.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation and egress policy.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MinerU is read-only on filesystem but uses MCP/API; open-webui has broad network egress, browser, subprocess, and mounted-volume access. They can both touch shared files and external services, so concurrent use can overwrite or misroute artifacts even without explicit git conflicts. The overlap is real but not as destructive as unrestricted shared writes.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same mounted directory, artifact races can occur.
IF open-webui subprocesses or tools mutate shared outputs while MinerU is reading them, conflicts arise.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent.
Make MinerU outputs immutable before open-webui reads them.
Pause open-webui background jobs during extraction runs.
Avoid shared mounted volumes for mutable artifacts.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces extracted text, tables, and OCR that open-webui can treat as chat context, documents, or tool input. open-webui is designed to act on such inputs via tools and function calling, so a bad extraction can cascade into incorrect downstream actions or summaries. Because verification is not enabled by default, the default path is dangerous.
conditions: IF open-webui uses MinerU output as authoritative input without a verification step, errors cascade.
IF downstream tools act on extracted facts, the cascade can affect external systems.
mitigations: Require human review before any action based on MinerU output.
Compare extracted fields against the source document for a sample set.
Disable action-taking tools for this workflow.
Mark MinerU output as untrusted in open-webui.
requires-engineering: add validation and confidence gating before tool execution.

E_compliance.rationale: MinerU is documented as private/offline and document-processing, while open-webui handles persistent memory, usage analytics, cloud connectors, and API keys. If regulated documents flow from MinerU into open-webui, retention and residency can diverge, creating a compliance mismatch. The risk is medium because the breach depends on the pair being used on the same sensitive corpus.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed through both agents, retention policies may diverge.
IF open-webui analytics or cloud connectors are enabled, residency and logging obligations can be violated.
mitigations: Disable analytics for regulated workflows.
Keep regulated documents out of open-webui unless retention is reviewed.
Use local-only connectors and offline mode where possible.
Document a retention policy for both agents.
requires-engineering: align residency, logging, and deletion controls.
